warnings.warning: The two-parameter CP critique motivates the three-parameter model, but four profile points do not establish physiological superiority or robust extrapolation.
Wprime, w, wrec, Padj, a, and b are not given a complete common unit and state-normalization convention.
The baseline dynamics treats rho as constant while the temperature section later changes rho; the two implementations are not reconciled.
The term u/(m v) is singular at v=0, yet the initial velocity and transition handling are not disclosed.
The effective-mass formula, drag term, and force notation mix bicycle/cyclist mass and acceleration units without a full dimensional closure.
vmax is held constant even for sharp turns, while braking is omitted, so turn feasibility is not physically represented.
PMP provides necessary conditions and four cases, but sufficiency, transversality, and boundary conditions are not demonstrated.
The Bellman/value-iteration pseudocode does not state state-grid resolution, action grid, transition probabilities, theta, runtime, or convergence diagnostics.
Wind drag Eq.36 names FW as drag force but divides by mass; units and directional sign conventions require reconciliation.
The pressure relation and temperature-altitude relation use unclear units and are not connected to an independent atmospheric calibration.
Temperature advice is inferred from a local 0.5 C sweep around 20 C and should not be generalized to extreme weather.
The team model defines front times and a fourth-rider objective but does not solve a schedule, enforce workload transitions, or calibrate Cdr.
Memo recommendations about hydration, equipment, psychological confidence, and following other players extend beyond the fitted model and safety evidence.
The PMP candidate set is presented as necessary, but no sufficiency or transversality verification is supplied.

global_organization_chain: An intuitive time-intensity contrast introduces the power curve and its race-planning purpose.
The prompt becomes three task blocks: profile/course, weather/deviation, and six-rider team optimization.
The literature review separates physiology models from dynamics and aerodynamic strategy models.
Four assumptions and a notation ledger define the measurement and motion boundary.
Training Peaks rider points and STRAVA route coordinates become fitted curves and discrete slope arrays.
Two- and three-parameter CP models explain profile differences before control is introduced.
Fatigue/recovery states and bicycle dynamics form a constrained state-space system.
PMP supplies candidate controls; Bellman recursion and DP supply a numerical policy.
Tokyo, UCI, and San Felice courses turn policies into power/elevation panels and finish-time tables.
Wind, temperature, deviation probability, and deviation location form separate sensitivity experiments.
Team drag reduction and lead duration become a six-rider fourth-finisher optimization formulation.
Strengths, weaknesses, and a two-page memo return the technical chain to race preparation.

main_argument_chains.claim: A three-parameter CP profile plus fatigue/recovery states can constrain a rider's feasible power over a course.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use rider-type pacing only for the sampled profile, course, constants, and state limits represented by the model.
support_steps: fit Eq.3-4 from four rider power horizons
define w and Padj in Eq.5-8
carry Pmax(w) into the control bound

main_argument_chains.claim: PMP and Bellman dynamic programming provide complementary analytic and numerical routes to a minimum-time pacing policy.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Keep necessary conditions, numerical policy, grid, and stopping details distinct when reproducing an optimizer.

main_argument_chains.claim: Weather and power-distribution sensitivity depends on route geometry and terrain location.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use wind and deviation guidance as route-specific operating advice, not global uncertainty bands.

main_argument_chains.claim: Team benefit is represented by position-dependent drag and lead-time decisions, but the six-rider extension remains a formulation.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Do not present a team rotation as optimized until the schedule solver, constraints, and calibration are supplied.
